title: Water-induced degradation and small-strain dynamic characteristics of tremella fuciformis polysaccharide treated loess
content:
by Shengting Shi, Haokun Tong, Jingxuan Zhou, Zhanpeng Ji, Xinlei Zhang

The susceptibility of loess to water-induced deterioration poses a major threat to geotechnical stability. This study investigates the small-strain dynamic behavior of loess treated with tremella fuciformis polysaccharide (TFP), a sustainable biopolymer, using resonant column tests. The evolution of the maximum shear modulus (Gmax) and reference shear strain (γr) was systematically analyzed under varying applied confining pressures, water contents, and TFP dosages. Results show that for untreated loess, Gmax follows a power-law growth with confining pressure and linear attenuation with water content. TFP treatment significantly bolsters the small-strain shear stiffness; at a 2% dosage (σc = 150 kPa, w = 13%), Gmax increases from 63.12 MPa to 139.93 MPa. TFP treatment enhances the initial shear stiffness while altering the reference shear strain, indicating changes in the strain-dependent modulus reduction characteristics. A unified multi-factor model was developed to characterize the variations in Gmax and γr, providing a quantitative description of the strain-dependent modulus reduction behavior. SEM observations reveal film-like and filament-like features around soil particles, suggesting microstructural changes associated with TFP treatment. These findings highlight the potential of TFP as a sustainable bio-based approach to enhance the small-strain shear stiffness of loess, particularly under high-water-content conditions.
